prompt: Sourced, partly reconstructed. Colour and tone from "Pluto Color Map" (PIA11707), NASA/JHUAPL/SwRI, public domain, https://www.jpl.nasa.gov/images/pia11707-pluto-color-map/. Detail from "Pluto New Horizons LORRI-MVIC Global Mosaic 300m" (July 2017), USGS Astrogeology Science Center, public domain, https://astrogeology.usgs.gov/search/map/pluto_new_horizons_lorri_mvic_global_mosaic_300m. Combined by pan-sharpening (the mosaic's fine detail over the colour map) and scaled to 4096x2048. On the far side, which New Horizons only saw at about 30 km per pixel, the fine relief is reconstructed: terrain texture taken from well-imaged cratered ground west of Sputnik Planitia is laid over the real colours and shapes there. That relief is not real. The black south, in polar night during the flyby, is filled from the northern hemisphere, mirrored across the equator and turned half a revolution; it is not real either.
